test_title: SSC CPO 2023 Official Paper-I (Held On: 04 Oct, 2023 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: How many fundamental rights were provided originally by the Indian Constitution in 1950?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Seven**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Constitution originally provided **seven main fundamental rights,** encompassing the right to equality, freedom, protection against exploitation, freedom of religion, cultural and educational rights, right to property, and the right to constitutional remedies.
 
• However, the right to property was removed from **Part III **of the Constitution through the **44th Amendment in 1978**.
 
• **Fundamental Rights**, enshrined in Part III of the Constitution, serve to uphold individual liberty and democratic principles grounded in the equality of all members of society.
 
• These rights guarantee civil liberties to all citizens and prevent the State from infringing upon individual liberty, while also obligating it to safeguard citizens' rights from encroachment by society.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Fundamental Rights, Directive Principles of State Policy, and Fundamental Duties **are integral components of the Constitution of India, delineating the fundamental obligations of the state towards its citizens and the reciprocal duties and rights of citizens towards the State.
 
• These provisions were crafted by the Constituent Assembly of India during the constitution-making process between 1949.
 
• Fundamental Rights, outlined in Part III of the Indian Constitution **(Articles 12 to 35), **ensure equality before the law and prohibit discrimination based on various factors such as race, place of birth, religion, caste, creed, sex, or gender. These rights are enforceable by the courts, with certain limitations.
 
• The **Directive Principles of State Policy,** laid down in Part IV of the Constitution, serve as guidelines for the government in formulating laws and policies.
